title: Finite discrete-valuation normalization and tame inertia character
statement: Let $A$ be a discrete valuation ring [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring] with fraction field $K$ and residue characteristic $p>0$. Let $L/K$ be a finite Galois field extension (finite, normal and separable), and let $B$ be the integral closure of $A$ in $L$ [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure]. Then $B$ is a finite $A$-module, and for every maximal ideal $\mathfrak n$ of $B$, the localization $B_{\mathfrak n}$ is a discrete valuation ring with fraction field $L$ and residue field $\kappa(\mathfrak n)$ finite over the residue field of $A$. Put $D=\{\sigma\in\operatorname{Gal}(L/K):\sigma(\mathfrak n)=\mathfrak n\}$ and $I=\{\sigma\in D:\sigma\text{ acts trivially on }\kappa(\mathfrak n)\}$. If $t$ is a uniformizer of $B_{\mathfrak n}$ and $e=v_{B_{\mathfrak n}}(\pi_A)$ is the ramification index for a uniformizer $\pi_A$ of $A$, the formula $\chi(\sigma)=\overline{\sigma(t)/t}$ defines a homomorphism $\chi:I\to\mu_e(\kappa(\mathfrak n))$, independent of $t$, where $\mu_e(E)=\{z\in E^\times:z^e=1\}$. Its kernel $P$ is normal in $D$ and is a finite $p$-group. If $n$ is the largest divisor of $e$ prime to $p$, then $\mu_e(\kappa(\mathfrak n))=\mu_n(\kappa(\mathfrak n))$ is cyclic of order $n$, and $\chi$ induces an isomorphism $I/P\cong\mu_n(\kappa(\mathfrak n))$.
